Step 1: two 4x10 plates are placed side by side along their long edges to form an 8x10 base; they only touch until the tiles bridge them.

Step 2: four 1x8 tiles form a border on the base. I assumed two tiles span the 8-wide ends, across both plates, and two run along the long sides, one on each plate. The 'Sears Tower' printed tile is on a long side, on one plate. The image is dark and the exact placement is uncertain.
Pieces and edges are listed in the output but the rests_on/other_joins structure is represented as joined edges (push-on) since the output schema has parts/edges.
Step 3: two light bluish gray 4x6 plates sit side by side in the 6x8 area inside the black tile border. Each spans both base plates b1 and b2.

Step 4: four light bluish gray 1x6 tiles form an inner border on the gray plates. I assumed two tiles span the 6-wide ends, one on each gray plate, and two run along the long sides across both gray plates. The picture shows only the first two tiles being placed.

Step 5: the callout shows a 2x2 plate, six 1x2 jumper plates, a long tile that I read as the 1x4 tile, and two small tiles that I read as 1x2 tiles. They fill the 4x6 inner area inside the gray tile border on top of the gray plates b7 and b8. The pictures are very dark, so the exact layout is a best guess.

Step 6: a 2x2 plate, a 1x2 brick and a 2x3 brick are added. The 2x2 plate is the second of the two in the parts list. Which pieces each one clutches below is uncertain, and the 1x2 brick is mostly hidden in the picture.
The output schema has parts and edges only, so 'rests_on' is recorded as joined push-on edges.

Step 7: a 1x3 brick (b26), a curved 2x2 brick (b27) and a 2x3 brick (b28) are added. The curved brick sits on the 2x2 plate b23. The 1x3 and 2x3 bricks sit on the earlier 2x3 brick b25 and 1x2 brick b24. The pictures are dark, so what each brick clutches below is a best guess.

Step 8: seven 1x3 bricks and seven 2x3 bricks build a tower. I read each layer as one 1x3 plus one 2x3 side by side, which gives a 3x3 footprint, and the layers are stacked 7 high. Each piece is assumed to rest on both pieces of the layer below, since the layer joints alternate (running bond). In each layer the 1x3 is the lower id (b29, b31 ... b41) and the 2x3 the higher id (b30, b32 ... b42).
The output schema has parts and edges only, so 'rests_on' is recorded as joined push-on edges.
Step 9: a 2x2 corner brick (b43) and a 2x2 brick (b44) go on top of the tower. I assumed the 2x2 brick sits on the top layer (b41, b42) and the corner brick sits on the 2x2 brick.

Step 10: two 1x1 tiles (b45, b46), a corner brick (b47) and a 2x2 brick (b48) are added. The tiles cover the studs left exposed by the corner bricks. I assumed b45 sits on b44 and b46 on b43. The corner b47 sits on b43 and b48 on b47. The dark picture makes the exact positions uncertain.
The output schema has parts and edges only, so 'rests_on' is recorded as joined push-on edges.

Step 11: a 1x1 tile (b49), a corner brick (b50) and a 2x2 brick (b51) go on top of the tower. The tile covers the stud left open beside the corner brick, so it sits on b48. The corner brick sits on b48 and the 2x2 brick on the corner brick.

Step 12: two 1x1 bricks (b52, b53), a 1x3 brick (b54) and a 1x1 tile (b55) form the stepped top. Their exact positions are hard to read in the dark picture, so what each clutches below is a best guess.
The output schema has parts and edges only, so 'rests_on' is recorded as joined push-on edges.
Steps 13 and 14 each add two 1x1 bricks and one 1x3 brick to the stepped top of the tower, so the two prongs grow one layer per step.

I assumed each new brick sits directly on the matching brick from the previous layer: b56 on b52, b57 on b53, b58 on b54, then b59 on b56, b60 on b57 and b61 on b58. The dark pictures make the exact positions uncertain.
The output schema has parts and edges only, so 'rests_on' is recorded as joined push-on edges.
Step 15: three 1x1 tiles (b62, b63, b64) cap the prong tops. I assumed b62 sits on b59, b63 on b60 and b64 on one stud of the 1x3 b61.

Step 16: three 1x2 bricks (b65, b66, b67) are stacked into the tall back column. I assumed b65 sits on the uncovered studs of b61, b66 on b65 and b67 on b66. The pictures are dark, so this placement is a best guess.
